children.text: On 17 January 2009 a camera recorded a meteor over the Baltic Sea. A 0.025 kg fragment was later found near Maribo. Use \(G=6.67\times10^{-11}\), Earth's mass \(m_E=5.97\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}\), radius \(R_E=6.38\times10^6\,\mathrm m\), Sun's mass \(m_S=1.99\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg}\), and Earth-Sun distance \(a_E=1.50\times10^{11}\,\mathrm m\). Stony material has \(c=1.2\times10^3\,\mathrm{J/(kg\,K)}\), conductivity \(k_s=2.0\,\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}\), density \(\rho=3.3\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), melting point \(T_m=1.7\times10^3\,\mathrm K\), and latent heat \(L=2.6\times10^5\,\mathrm{J/kg}\). During atmospheric heating, take the surface temperature to be a constant \(1000\,\mathrm K\).

children.text: The meteor travels on a straight track heading \(285^\circ\) clockwise from north towards the landing site, 195 km from the camera at azimuth \(230^\circ\). Frame 155 at 1.46 s has azimuth \(215^\circ\), altitude \(19.2^\circ\). Frame 161 at 2.28 s has azimuth \(221^\circ\), altitude \(14.7^\circ\). Find its mean speed, neglecting Earth curvature and gravity.

An entering sphere has mass \(m_M=30\,\mathrm{kg}\), radius \(R_M=0.13\,\mathrm m\), temperature \(T_0=200\,\mathrm K\), and speed \(v_M=2.91\times10^4\,\mathrm{m/s}\). Drag is \(F=k\rho_{\rm atm}Av^2\), with \(k=0.60\), \(\rho_{\rm atm}=4.1\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), and \(A=\pi R_M^2\). Estimate time to slow to \(0.90v_M\), keeping shape and mass fixed and ignoring gravity.
Find initial kinetic energy divided by the energy needed to melt the sphere completely.
Only an outer layer is heated while the surface stays at constant high temperature. Use dimensional analysis on \(x\sim t^\alpha\rho^\beta c^\gamma k_s^\delta\) to determine all four powers.

children.text: Write the decay of \(^{87}_{37}\mathrm{Rb}\) to \(^{87}_{38}\mathrm{Sr}\). The Rb half-life is \(4.9\times10^{10}\) years.

At crystallization, all minerals have the same \(^{87}\mathrm{Sr}/{}^{86}\mathrm{Sr}\), but different \(^{87}\mathrm{Rb}/{}^{86}\mathrm{Sr}\). Show that their present ratios form a line of slope \(e^{\lambda t}-1\).
Read the slope from the original isochron graph and find the age.
Comet Encke has minimum and maximum solar distances \(4.95\times10^{10}\,\mathrm m\) and \(6.16\times10^{11}\,\mathrm m\). Find its period.

An asteroid of density \(3.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), radius 5.0 km and impact speed \(2.5\times10^4\,\mathrm{m/s}\) strikes the North Pole in a completely inelastic collision. Earth has inertia \(I_E=0.83(2/5)m_ER_E^2\). Find the maximum axis tilt. Neglect orbital changes and use a 24 h initial day.
For the same asteroid, find the change in day length for a radial equatorial impact.
Find the change in day length for a prograde tangential equatorial impact. Also discuss the opposite direction.
Find the largest surface impact speed of a body initially gravitationally bound to the solar system. Ignore atmosphere, other bodies and Earth rotation.

statement.text:
The Maribo Meteorite
On 17 January 2009 a camera recorded a meteor over the Baltic Sea. A 0.025 kg fragment was later found near Maribo. Use \(G=6.67\times10^{-11}\), Earth's mass \(m_E=5.97\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}\), radius \(R_E=6.38\times10^6\,\mathrm m\), Sun's mass \(m_S=1.99\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg}\), and Earth-Sun distance \(a_E=1.50\times10^{11}\,\mathrm m\). Stony material has \(c=1.2\times10^3\,\mathrm{J/(kg\,K)}\), conductivity \(k_s=2.0\,\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}\), density \(\rho=3.3\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), melting point \(T_m=1.7\times10^3\,\mathrm K\), and latent heat \(L=2.6\times10^5\,\mathrm{J/kg}\). During atmospheric heating, take the surface temperature to be a constant \(1000\,\mathrm K\).
1.1. Camera speed

The meteor travels on a straight track heading \(285^\circ\) clockwise from north towards the landing site, 195 km from the camera at azimuth \(230^\circ\). Frame 155 at 1.46 s has azimuth \(215^\circ\), altitude \(19.2^\circ\). Frame 161 at 2.28 s has azimuth \(221^\circ\), altitude \(14.7^\circ\). Find its mean speed, neglecting Earth curvature and gravity.
1.2a. Atmospheric deceleration
An entering sphere has mass \(m_M=30\,\mathrm{kg}\), radius \(R_M=0.13\,\mathrm m\), temperature \(T_0=200\,\mathrm K\), and speed \(v_M=2.91\times10^4\,\mathrm{m/s}\). Drag is \(F=k\rho_{\rm atm}Av^2\), with \(k=0.60\), \(\rho_{\rm atm}=4.1\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), and \(A=\pi R_M^2\). Estimate time to slow to \(0.90v_M\), keeping shape and mass fixed and ignoring gravity.
1.2b. Energy available for melting
Find initial kinetic energy divided by the energy needed to melt the sphere completely.
1.3a. Thermal penetration powers
Only an outer layer is heated while the surface stays at constant high temperature. Use dimensional analysis on \(x\sim t^\alpha\rho^\beta c^\gamma k_s^\delta\) to determine all four powers.
1.3b. Heated-layer thickness
Find \(x\) and \(x/R_M\) after 5 s.
1.4a. Radioactive decay scheme

Write the decay of \(^{87}_{37}\mathrm{Rb}\) to \(^{87}_{38}\mathrm{Sr}\). The Rb half-life is \(4.9\times10^{10}\) years.
1.4b. Isochron proof
At crystallization, all minerals have the same \(^{87}\mathrm{Sr}/{}^{86}\mathrm{Sr}\), but different \(^{87}\mathrm{Rb}/{}^{86}\mathrm{Sr}\). Show that their present ratios form a line of slope \(e^{\lambda t}-1\).
1.4c. Radiometric age
Read the slope from the original isochron graph and find the age.
1.5. Comet Encke period
Comet Encke has minimum and maximum solar distances \(4.95\times10^{10}\,\mathrm m\) and \(6.16\times10^{11}\,\mathrm m\). Find its period.
1.6a. Maximum pole-impact tilt
An asteroid of density \(3.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), radius 5.0 km and impact speed \(2.5\times10^4\,\mathrm{m/s}\) strikes the North Pole in a completely inelastic collision. Earth has inertia \(I_E=0.83(2/5)m_ER_E^2\). Find the maximum axis tilt. Neglect orbital changes and use a 24 h initial day.
1.6b. Radial equatorial impact
For the same asteroid, find the change in day length for a radial equatorial impact.
1.6c. Tangential equatorial impact
Find the change in day length for a prograde tangential equatorial impact. Also discuss the opposite direction.
1.7. Maximum impact speed
Find the largest surface impact speed of a body initially gravitationally bound to the solar system. Ignore atmosphere, other bodies and Earth rotation.

children.text: Intersect each horizontal camera bearing with the line through the landing site heading \(285^\circ\). The horizontal camera ranges are \(195\sin55^\circ/\sin70^\circ\) and \(195\sin55^\circ/\sin64^\circ\) km. Their heights are these ranges times \(\tan19.2^\circ\) and \(\tan14.7^\circ\). Combine the horizontal track displacement with the height difference and divide by \(0.82\,\mathrm s\). The result is about \(29.1\,\mathrm{km/s}\).
The dimensions of heat conduction give \(x=\sqrt{k_st/(\rho c)}\). Thus \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)=(1/2,-1/2,-1/2,1/2)\).

Rb decays as \(N_R(t)=N_R(0)e^{-\lambda t}\), while daughter Sr increases by \(N_R(0)-N_R(t)\). Divide by stable \(N_{86}\): \[\frac{N_{87\rm Sr}(t)}{N_{86}}=\frac{N_{87\rm Sr}(0)}{N_{86}}+(e^{\lambda t}-1)\frac{N_R(t)}{N_{86}}.\] This is the requested straight line with a common intercept.
The graph rises from approximately 0.700 to 0.712 over a horizontal span 0.25. Its slope is about 0.050. Therefore \(t=T_{1/2}\ln(1+a)/\ln2=3.4\times10^9\) years.
Its semi-major axis is the mean of the two distances. Kepler's law gives \(T=2\pi\sqrt{a^3/(Gm_S)}=3.30\) years.

The asteroid mass is \(1.57\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{kg}\). Its largest angular momentum is \(m_av_aR_E\), perpendicular to Earth's spin. Hence \(\Delta\theta\simeq m_av_aR_E/(I_E\omega_E)=4.27\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm{rad}\).
No angular momentum is added, but \(\Delta I=m_aR_E^2\). Thus \(\Delta T\simeq T\Delta I/I_E=6.84\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm s\).

Use \((I_E+m_aR_E^2)\omega_f=I_E\omega_E+m_av_aR_E\). To first order, \(\Delta T/T=\Delta I/I_E-\Delta L/L_E\), giving \(-3.62\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm s\). A retrograde impact changes the angular-momentum term's sign and lengthens the day.

The largest heliocentric speed at Earth's orbit approaches solar escape speed \(\sqrt{2Gm_S/a_E}\). A head-on encounter adds Earth's orbital speed \(\sqrt{Gm_S/a_E}\). Earth's gravity then adds escape-speed squared: \[v_{\max}=\sqrt{(\sqrt2+1)^2Gm_S/a_E+2Gm_E/R_E}\simeq72.8\,\mathrm{km/s}.\]

solution.text:
The Maribo Meteorite
1.1. Camera speed
Intersect each horizontal camera bearing with the line through the landing site heading \(285^\circ\). The horizontal camera ranges are \(195\sin55^\circ/\sin70^\circ\) and \(195\sin55^\circ/\sin64^\circ\) km. Their heights are these ranges times \(\tan19.2^\circ\) and \(\tan14.7^\circ\). Combine the horizontal track displacement with the height difference and divide by \(0.82\,\mathrm s\). The result is about \(29.1\,\mathrm{km/s}\).
1.2a. Atmospheric deceleration
Integrate \(m_M\dot v=-k\rho_{\rm atm}Av^2\): \[t=\frac{m_M}{k\rho_{\rm atm}\pi R_M^2v_M}\left(\frac1{0.9}-1\right)\simeq0.88\,\mathrm s.\]
1.2b. Energy available for melting
The mass cancels: \[\frac{E_{\rm kin}}{E_{\rm melt}}=\frac{v_M^2/2}{c(T_m-T_0)+L}\simeq2.1\times10^2.\]
1.3a. Thermal penetration powers
The dimensions of heat conduction give \(x=\sqrt{k_st/(\rho c)}\). Thus \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)=(1/2,-1/2,-1/2,1/2)\).
1.3b. Heated-layer thickness
\(x=\sqrt{k_st/(\rho c)}=1.6\,\mathrm{mm}\), and \(x/R_M=0.012\).
1.4a. Radioactive decay scheme
\[{}^{87}_{37}\mathrm{Rb}\longrightarrow{}^{87}_{38}\mathrm{Sr}+{}^0_{-1}e+\bar\nu_e.\] This is beta-minus decay.
1.4b. Isochron proof
Rb decays as \(N_R(t)=N_R(0)e^{-\lambda t}\), while daughter Sr increases by \(N_R(0)-N_R(t)\). Divide by stable \(N_{86}\): \[\frac{N_{87\rm Sr}(t)}{N_{86}}=\frac{N_{87\rm Sr}(0)}{N_{86}}+(e^{\lambda t}-1)\frac{N_R(t)}{N_{86}}.\] This is the requested straight line with a common intercept.
1.4c. Radiometric age
The graph rises from approximately 0.700 to 0.712 over a horizontal span 0.25. Its slope is about 0.050. Therefore \(t=T_{1/2}\ln(1+a)/\ln2=3.4\times10^9\) years.
1.5. Comet Encke period
Its semi-major axis is the mean of the two distances. Kepler's law gives \(T=2\pi\sqrt{a^3/(Gm_S)}=3.30\) years.
1.6a. Maximum pole-impact tilt
The asteroid mass is \(1.57\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{kg}\). Its largest angular momentum is \(m_av_aR_E\), perpendicular to Earth's spin. Hence \(\Delta\theta\simeq m_av_aR_E/(I_E\omega_E)=4.27\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm{rad}\).
1.6b. Radial equatorial impact
No angular momentum is added, but \(\Delta I=m_aR_E^2\). Thus \(\Delta T\simeq T\Delta I/I_E=6.84\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm s\).
1.6c. Tangential equatorial impact
Use \((I_E+m_aR_E^2)\omega_f=I_E\omega_E+m_av_aR_E\). To first order, \(\Delta T/T=\Delta I/I_E-\Delta L/L_E\), giving \(-3.62\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm s\). A retrograde impact changes the angular-momentum term's sign and lengthens the day.
1.7. Maximum impact speed
The largest heliocentric speed at Earth's orbit approaches solar escape speed \(\sqrt{2Gm_S/a_E}\). A head-on encounter adds Earth's orbital speed \(\sqrt{Gm_S/a_E}\). Earth's gravity then adds escape-speed squared: \[v_{\max}=\sqrt{(\sqrt2+1)^2Gm_S/a_E+2Gm_E/R_E}\simeq72.8\,\mathrm{km/s}.\]
